---
title: "Research"
description: "Deep learning for time-series classification, applied to human activity recognition from wearable sensors."
---

My doctoral research developed **TSCResNet**, a one-dimensional residual convolutional network for time-series classification, and applied it to recognizing human activities from wearable-sensor data. I studied it first in the closed-set setting, where every activity is seen during training, and then in the open-set setting, where the model must also recognize activities it has never seen. Code and details are on the [project page](projects/tscresnet.md).

## Publications

::: {.pub}
[Performance Evaluation of Open-Set Classification in Human Activity Recognition via a Residual Neural Network Architecture]{.pub-title}\
[D. Rodriguez Gonzalez, Y. Qu · *2023 Congress in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, & Applied Computing (CSCE)*, IEEE, pp. 470–476, 2023]{.pub-venue}

Applies TSCResNet to open-set activity recognition, where some activities are absent from training, a situation common in real deployments but little studied. Evaluated on the PAMAP2 benchmark with the same preprocessing and protocol as prior open-set work.

[[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1109/CSCE60160.2023.00084){aria-label="DOI for the 2023 CSCE open-set paper"}]{.pub-links}
:::

::: {.pub}
[Improving the Performance of Closed-Set Classification in Human Activity Recognition by Applying a Residual Neural Network Architecture]{.pub-title}\
[D. Rodriguez Gonzalez, Y. Qu · *European Journal of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science* 6(2), 59–65, 2022 · Open access (CC BY 4.0)]{.pub-venue}

Introduces TSCResNet and evaluates it on the PAMAP2 benchmark using the standard held-out-subject protocol, reaching 95.6% accuracy and 95.5% mean F1, above the prior results it was compared against (best: 93.7% accuracy).

[[DOI](https://doi.org/10.24018/ejece.2022.6.2.433){aria-label="DOI for the 2022 EJECE closed-set paper"} [PDF](https://eu-opensci.org/index.php/ejece/article/download/19433/11229){aria-label="PDF of the 2022 EJECE closed-set paper"}]{.pub-links}
:::

::: {.pub}
[Improving the Performance of Open-Set Classification in Human Activity Recognition by Applying a Residual Neural Network Architecture]{.pub-title}\
[D. Rodriguez Gonzalez · Doctor of Computer Science dissertation, Colorado Technical University, 2022]{.pub-venue}

[[ProQuest](https://www.proquest.com/openview/1bcde6c7e49e9b389272c22dfbd48346/1){aria-label="Dissertation on ProQuest"}]{.pub-links}
